learning_outcomes.text: Knowledge in basic and technological subjects, enabling them to learn new methods and theories, and providing them with versatility to adapt to new situations.
Ability to solve problems with initiative, decision-making, creativity, and critical reasoning.
Ability to communicate and transmit knowledge, skills, and aptitudes in the field of Industrial Organization Engineering, both orally and in writing, and to all types of audiences.
Ability to handle specifications, regulations, and mandatory standards.
Ability to apply quality principles and methods.
Ability to organize and plan in the business environment, and other institutions and organizations.
Ability for the prevention of occupational risks and protection of the health and safety of workers and users.
Honesty, responsibility, ethical commitment, and solidarity spirit.
Ability to work in a team.
Ability to know, select, critique, and use diverse sources of information.
Acquire knowledge and capabilities for process management, monitoring, and improvement.
Know, develop, and integrate business management systems.
Understand and know how to use basic and advanced process management tools.
Know the most frequently used management systems and the fundamentals for their certification.
Design and implement integrated management systems.
Know how to apply variable and attribute control charts and continuous process improvement methodologies.

syllabus_topics: Evolution of fundamental concepts and principles of quality
The basic legal framework for occupational risk prevention
Occupational risk prevention policy and preventive culture
Health and safety plan or occupational risk prevention management system
The UNE ISO 14001:2015 standard and the environmental management system
Concepts of circular economy and sustainability
Definition and determining factors of CSR
The UNE-ISO 22301:2019 standard for business continuity management
Application of the integration of management systems
teaching_methods: Practical application of theoretical content by students
Daily summary of previous content by a rotating student volunteer
Individual, pair, or group work during classroom practices
Creation and maintenance of an individual portfolio (PA) for classroom practice tasks
Group work (TG) in laboratory sessions to design an integrated management system
assessment_rules: The final grade is calculated as 0.3 * TG + 0.2 * PA + 0.5 * TEST. It is essential to attend at least 80% of both practical classes and laboratory practices. An incomplete portfolio (PA) will invalidate that part, resulting in a zero for that 20% of the grade. Students in differentiated evaluation or extraordinary examination must complete the portfolio (PA) and the basic knowledge test (TEST). For the extraordinary examination, if the group work (TG) was presented during continuous assessment, its original score will be used; otherwise, the document must be submitted electronically and in paper format at least three days before the extraordinary exam date, followed by a maximum 15-minute presentation after the test.
